name: life
breaks_up: an animal's life, by whether each part of it is the animal's own or taken by use
left_out: What an animal means, intends or feels. The syntax names what is the animal's own and what is taken by use, never what its signals mean; they are read for structure, never translated. Things and people hold no part of it: every part is the animal's.

elements.name: its own ground
elements.description: where it goes by itself, free at the time

elements.name: confined
elements.description: captured, or kept where people put it

element_types.name: food
element_types.description: What the animal eats, and who brings it.

elements.name: found by itself
elements.description: what it finds and takes on its own

elements.name: fed
elements.description: given food by people, which ties it to them

elements.name: trained or rewarded
elements.description: shaped by people towards something they want

elements.name: unmarked
elements.description: as it is, carrying nothing people put on it

elements.name: tagged
elements.description: marked or fitted so that people can find or identify it

element_types.name: signal
element_types.description: What the animal makes heard or seen.

elements.name: its own, read for structure
elements.description: units, sequence and rhythm, never put into human words

elements.name: translated
elements.description: turned into a human word, as if the animal were a text to be read

instances.name: Split-Domain Cognition's animal-rights variant
instances.what: the rights position the syntax is read from: whether a use of an animal should exist, never how well the animal is treated inside it
